methods.label: Compare the loss with the watch's indicated elapsed time
methods.explanation:
The final time in the question is shown by the slow watch, so we need the ratio of the accumulated loss to the elapsed time indicated by the watch.

From March 15 at 1 P.M. to March 21 at 9 A.M., the indicated elapsed time is six days minus four hours:
\[
6\cdot24-4=140\text{ hours}=8400\text{ minutes}.
\]
During each actual day of \(1440\) minutes, the watch advances only \(1440-5/2\) minutes, while the required correction grows by \(5/2\) minutes. At the stated constant rate, these quantities remain proportional. Since the watch was initially correct,
\[
\frac{n}{8400}
=\frac{5/2}{1440-5/2}
=\frac{1}{575}.
\]
Therefore
\[
n=\frac{8400}{575}=\frac{336}{23}
=\boxed{14\frac{14}{23}\text{ minutes}},
\]
choice A.
